questions.q: What is Azure Monitor, in the terms this lesson uses?
options: A command-line tool that only reports VM CPU usage
A third-party product that must be installed separately from Azure
The umbrella platform underneath Log Analytics, Application Insights, Container Insights, and alerting — not one standalone tool
A single dashboard product that replaces Log Analytics and Application Insights
questions.explain: Azure Monitor is the platform that every other monitoring feature in this chapter is built on top of; it isn't a single pane of glass itself.

questions.q: Why are Azure Monitor platform metrics cheap and fast to query compared to logs?
options: Because metrics are numeric, pre-aggregated time-series values in a dedicated store, not free-form structured records
Because metrics are stored for only ten minutes before deletion
Because metrics are never collected automatically, so there is less data overall
Because metrics are stored in the same table format as Perf logs
questions.explain: The metrics store is purpose-built for numeric time-series data, which is what makes it cheap to store and fast enough for live dashboards and high-frequency alerting.

questions.q: A team says a resource's diagnostic logs "just aren't showing up" in their Log Analytics workspace. What is the most likely cause, per this lesson?
options: Log Analytics workspaces cannot store resource logs at all
The Activity Log automatically blocks all resource logs by default
KQL queries cannot read resource logs, only platform metrics
No diagnostic setting was ever configured on that resource to route its logs to the workspace
questions.explain: Most resource (data-plane) logs are never captured anywhere queryable until a diagnostic setting on that specific resource routes them to a workspace, storage account, or Event Hub.

questions.q: What is the Activity Log, and how is it different from a resource's diagnostic logs?
options: It is a custom _CL table that must be created manually before any data appears
It is the subscription-level record of control-plane (write) operations, retained 90 days automatically with no diagnostic setting required
It only exists after Application Insights is enabled on a resource
It is a numeric metric, not a log, and lives in the metrics store
questions.explain: Unlike most resource logs, the Activity Log is automatically retained at the subscription level for 90 days and needs no diagnostic setting to be visible.

questions.q: You need to answer "is something wrong right now" across dozens of resources on a live dashboard. Which tool fits that question best, and why?
options: A diagnostic setting, because it directly renders charts
A log alert, because log alerts always evaluate faster than metric alerts
Metrics Explorer, because metrics are cheap, pre-aggregated, and fast enough to scan across many resources in seconds
Container Insights, because it is the only feature that can read the Activity Log
questions.explain: Metrics Explorer is built for exactly this: fast, cheap, high-frequency numeric data that scans well across many resources, which is why it backs live dashboards and fast alert rules.
